what: Imprinting runs with the work: rooms mark, record and begin to carry on their work while it is being built, and they mark and record an attempt cut short or lost, not only once the work is up and near the close.
change: Bounds on P11 and P13 and wider bounds on A07, A08 and A09. P11 ('When a work is up, the room marks it') would add: the room also marks partial progress, an unfinished attempt and a lost work, and members dispute credit while the work goes on. P13 ('Near the close and after it') would add: carrying on can begin while placement is live. The bounds of A07 (the late find and the work the close cut short), A08 (the late side) and A09 (a next canvas planned while still building) would widen to the whole course of the work. The arrows' statements and their order counts (A07 139 of 182 rooms, A08 225 of 289, A09 113 of 145) are not changed: the order holds in most rooms, and the proposal bounds where it does not.
why: Four forms change the dimension. P11 is specified by A (21 of 135 defining rooms) and D (15 of 96); P13 by D (30 of 96); A07 is restricted by E (14 of 84) and F (7 of 34), A08 by E (24) and A09 by D (16) and E (10); P12 is specified by F's links (5). In 46 of these rooms the line says the act came during the work, before a finish, or after the work was cut short or lost (my reading). Branches F17, F18 and F19 (marking and credit while the work goes on), F11 (carrying on begun before the close) and F09 (rooms that moved mark an unfinished work) explain parts of it. The D5 notes found the same: A07's bound does not cover marking during the work, before its finish, after its loss or on a spot held on leave (18 rooms across F27, F30 and F31), and many A09 restrict lines deny a causal role the arrow does not claim.
